Applying the definition of variance and using the linearity of expectation, we have

Content:
[MATH: Var[X + Y]|= E[((X + Y) − E[X + Y])^{2}]; = E[((X − E[X]) + (Y − E[Y]))^{2}]; = E[(X − E[X])^{2} + (Y − E[Y])^{2} + 2(X − E[X])(Y − E[Y])].]

Distributing the expected value, and using the fact that [MATH: \textrm{E}[aX] = a\cdot \textrm{E}[X]] for constant [MATH: a,] we have

[MATH: Var[X + Y]|= E[(X − E[X])^{2} + (Y − E[Y])^{2} + 2(X − E[X])(Y − E[Y])]; = E[(X − E[X])^{2}] + E[(Y − E[Y])^{2}] + 2 ⋅ E[(X − E[X])(Y − E[Y])]; = Var[X] + Var[Y] + 2Cov[X, Y]]
